MeshNavarra Utility User Manual

 1. Connect: connect your Meshtastic node via USB OTG ("Discover & Connect") or via Bluetooth ("Connect via Bluetooth", choose the paired node). The NodeDB downloads automatically and the node list populates.

 2. Tabs (bottom bar): Good Practices, Commands, Administration, NavaTastic CLI, Chat, Nodes and Log. Swipe or tap to move between them; the edge arrows show there are more tabs. The first few times you open a tab, a popup explains what it is for.

 3. Administration: target a node by ID or with the list button, then Reboot, Wipe NodeDB (with Keep Favorites), Set Favorite or Set Ignored. "Get Node Info" redownloads the database.

 4. Commands: request Telemetry, Position, Traceroute or Set Owner Name on the chosen node; you can also send a free text message. Each action shows a popup with the decoded response.

 5. Nodes: visual cards with every node (favorites first) — battery, voltage, SNR, last heard and hops.

 6. Good Practices: applies optimized transmit timings (hop 5, NodeInfo and GPS beacon every 72 h, smart position off, GPS off) via safe read-modify-write to the selected node.

 7. Chat: see the node's stored messages and live ones, and reply on the channel. Use Pause before sending administration commands.

 8. NavaTastic CLI: remote control for a NavaTastic repeater (requires the custom Navarrico/NavaTastic firmware on the target node — see the intro popup when you open the tab). Choose the target node, the route (Navadmin or private DM), the category and the command; press "?" on any command to see what it does and its usage. The argument field adapts to the command (text, number, node ID or option list) and the preview line shows exactly what will be sent. Read-only commands can use the Navadmin channel; control commands are only allowed as encrypted direct messages to the chosen node. If the Navadmin channel is missing, the app offers to create it. The conversation (Navadmin + DM) is kept on disk.

 9. Log: persistent record of every request and response with timestamps.

 Note: this is an unofficial fork. Remote administration may be rejected by newer firmware unless the PKC session key is established; the app is provided AS IS (see disclaimer).

This app has a hidden developer tab with low-impact mode, sensor toggles and radio test options. It is disabled by default. Show it?
Test tools: low-impact mode and LoRa overrides (hop limit, frequency, duty cycle). These change things you normally never touch — use only in a test band, away from the production mesh.

Why follow the Good Practices? Because the 868 MHz ISM band is shared, legally limited and already full of users in Spain.

The band is regulated by ETSI EN 300 220 and split into sub-bands, each with a maximum DUTY CYCLE: the fraction of time a device may transmit. If you transmit 1 second, you must stay silent long enough to respect the limit of that sub-band.

ETSI sub-bands and duty cycle (EN 300 220-2, §4.3.3):
- 863-865 MHz: 0.1%
- 865-868 MHz: 1%
- 868-868.6 MHz: 1% (the usual Meshtastic default in Spain is 868.1 MHz)
- 868.7-869.2 MHz: 0.1%
- 869.4-869.65 MHz: 10% (up to 500 mW ERP; the Navarrico fleet runs here, SFNarrow 869.618 MHz)
- 869.7-870 MHz: 1%

The limit is per device and per sub-band, and it is the OPERATOR's responsibility: exceeding it is not just bad manners, it is illegal and degrades the network for everyone.

There are already thousands of Meshtastic nodes in Spain. Every node periodically sends beacons: NodeInfo (name), device telemetry and GPS position. With thousands of nodes that background traffic adds up to a lot of airtime. User messages are worth far more than beacons — this tab reduces beacon traffic to the minimum needed to stay visible in the mesh:
- NodeInfo every 72 h instead of 3 h (24x less)
- GPS position every 72 h with smart position OFF (no extra bursts)
- Sensible hop limit and rebroadcast settings

If we all do this, the channel stays mostly free for real messages. Apply it to your own node and encourage the rest of the fleet to do the same.

References:
- ETSI EN 300 220-1 / -2 (short-range devices; duty cycle in EN 300 220-2 §4.3.3)
- The Things Network — Duty Cycle: https://www.thethingsnetwork.org/docs/lorawan/duty-cycle/
- Meshtastic: https://meshtastic.org

The target node must run the custom Navarrico/NavaTastic firmware (a Meshtastic fork). Official Meshtastic firmware does NOT understand /nava commands.

What it is: a Meshtastic v2.7.26 fork optimized for solar infrastructure repeaters (SFNarrow mesh, EU868). The NavaCLIModule adds remote fleet management over /nava commands: read-only queries on the Navadmin channel and control via PKI-encrypted private DMs.

Improvements over the official firmware:
- Real System OFF (1-3 µA) with hardware LPCOMP wake; survives solar brownout with waitUntilPowerLevelSafe + hysteresis.
- Flash protection: NodeDB kept in RAM, auto-favorites (RAM-only) and selective saving to extend flash life.
- Remote admin with up to 3 PKI keys; the Navadmin channel is read-only and never answers non-admins.
- Full remote control: battery chemistry, shutdown/wake voltages (vbat/vwake), storm hibernation, hot config (name/role/mqtt/tz/hops/txpower), maintenance (db_*, reboot, factory_reset), TX on/off and BLE.
- Solar-friendly defaults: Router role, manual EU868 radio (SFNarrow), NodeInfo and position every 72 h, tuned ADC multiplier.
- Favorites hop-bypass and fleet addressing (!ID, @role, @name, all).

Pick the target node (favorites first) and send. Control commands go as encrypted DMs; read-only ones may use the Navadmin channel.
This will be sent to the REAL node. A wrong value can leave the node unusable until you recover it physically. Type CONFIRMAR to enable sending.
The Navadmin channel (name "Navadmin", PSK AQ==) was not detected on this node. It is needed to receive the read-only command responses. Create it now (first free secondary channel slot)?
Only the primary channel (slot 0) exists; it cannot be reused.
Slot %1$d is "%2$s". Reuse it as the Navadmin channel (it will be renamed and its PSK replaced), or disable it first and then create Navadmin in the freed slot.
Channel slot %1$d disabled; creating Navadmin next.
Choose which channel to send your reply on (SFNarrow, Navadmin, or any other channel the node has). Received messages are grouped by channel — tap a channel header to expand/collapse it.

Empty targets the connected node. Pick from the NodeDB to configure a remote node (your public key must be in its admin list). Remote applies the sequence over the mesh: 3 commands (hops, NodeInfo, position) sent in order — the protocol has no single "apply everything" message, so the app chains them automatically.

Applies optimized transmit timings for background information (node info, GPS beacons, position) so the mesh keeps most of its airtime for user messages. Defaults: hop limit 5, node info and GPS beacon every 72 hours, smart position off, GPS off (re-enable it later if you need tracking).
Low-impact: no saved config to restore (enable it first).

Sets the primary channel (name + PSK) and the LoRa preset. Stock presets reset the channel slot and clear the frequency override; SFN Spain applies the SFNarrow values (869.618 MHz, 62 kHz, SF7, CR5, slot 4).
Override duty cycle (100%, test band only)
Sensor toggles apply to the connected node on change.
Enables/disables the node\'s environment sensor (BME680): temperature, humidity and pressure telemetry, plus air quality if available. Applies to the connected node with read-modify-write.
Enables/disables the node\'s power/energy sensor (INA219/260): bus voltage, current and power telemetry. Generic — works on any node that has the sensor; nodes without it simply report no data.

Low-impact mode: caps every packet this app sends at 1 hop and forces the node to 1 hop. Use it to keep tests quiet on shared channels. NOTE: disabling it must restore the node\'s previous hops and frequency.
Sets the node\'s LoRa hop limit (1-7) via read-modify-write of the LORA section. Re-tune after a factory reset.
Sets the node\'s radio frequency (863.0-870.0 MHz) via read-modify-write. Used for the isolated test band (869.545). Requires a node reboot to re-tune.
Overrides the duty-cycle limit (100% = no TX limit). Test band only — never enable on a production channel.
Runs the selected automated audit battery (Navadmin, Commands, Admin local/remote, Chat, DM control, Config get). Results go to the popup and an audit file.
Selects which automated audit battery to run: Navadmin (read-only B), Commands (B), Admin local (A), Chat (B), Admin remote PKI (B), DM control (B, safe), Config get (A, read-only).
Applies the selected radio preset (SFN Spain or a stock modem preset) to the node via read-modify-write.
Radio presets: SFN Spain (869.618 MHz, the Navarrico fleet band) or stock modem presets (LONG/SHORT × FAST/SLOW/TURBO). The preset defines bandwidth, spread factor, coding rate and channel.
NavaTastic command category: Diagnostics, Blocks, Favorites, Configuration, Maintenance, Power, Transmission, Utilities. Read-only commands work on the Navadmin channel; control commands use PKI DM.
The specific /nava command to send. Commands with ⚠ are destructive and require typing CONFIRMAR. Long-press any entry to see its description inline.
Extra argument for the selected command (e.g. storm test1/2, battery chemistry, hops). Some commands need no option.
LoRa hop limit (1-7) to apply to the node via read-modify-write. Lower = less rebroadcast airtime; the test band uses 1.
Radio frequency in MHz (863.0-870.0) to apply via read-modify-write, e.g. 869.545 for the isolated test band. A node reboot re-tunes the radio.

Sends the selected NavaTastic command via the chosen route (Navadmin = read-only, DM = control). Warn commands require CONFIRMAR.

Imports a node\'s business card from a Meshtastic shared URL (https://meshtastic.org/v/#...). The card is stored in the app\'s own node cache (not in the node\'s NodeDB, which only holds 80 entries). If the URL has no PKI key, the app forces a user-info exchange with the node to learn it.
… and %1$d more in cache (connect a node to refresh)
Long-press any button to see this help. Full details are in the user manual (the "?" button).

Connect the phone to a Meshtastic node with a USB OTG cable and accept the USB permission dialog. The NodeDB (up to 80 nodes) downloads automatically. Tip: USB keeps the node powered and is the fastest way to administer it.
Connect to the node over Bluetooth. The NodeDB download is slower than USB. Tip: on Android 12+, grant the location permission for scanning; after bonding once, reconnects are faster.
Re-downloads MyNodeInfo, configuration, channels and the NodeDB (equivalent of "meshtastic --info"). Use it to refresh the node list after changes.
Reboots the target node (10 s delay — the ACK is sent first). Tip: the node re-broadcasts its NodeInfo on boot, which helps other nodes update its key/name.
Wipes the target node\'s NodeDB. With "Keep Favorites" checked, favorites survive. Tip: run it before tests to start clean — the node re-learns its neighbors from the mesh.
Factory reset of the target node (Navarrico firmware restores the rescue channels). Remote access is lost by design: keep USB access to recover.
Marks the node as favorite in the target\'s NodeDB. Favorites are never evicted (even at 80 nodes) and bypass hop limits on Navarrico routers.
Removes the node from the target\'s favorites list.
Mutes the node: its messages are no longer shown. Tip: check the ID carefully — ignoring an admin can block remote management.
Unmutes the node (removes it from the ignored list).
Removes a node entry (and its key) from the NodeDB without rebooting. Use it to clear a stale key before a factory reset so both nodes re-handshake and exchange keys.
Use NavaCLI for these requests (PKI DM)
Requests the node\'s user info and exchanges NodeInfo so both sides learn each other\'s public key (needed for PKI). With NavaCLI: /nava nodeinfo.
Requests device telemetry (battery, voltage, channel utilization). With NavaCLI: /nava sendtel.
Requests environment metrics (temperature/humidity/pressure) from the node\'s I2C sensor. With NavaCLI: /nava env.
Requests power/energy metrics (voltage, current). With NavaCLI: /nava power.
Requests the node\'s GPS position. With NavaCLI: /nava pos.
Runs a traceroute to the node showing the hop path there and back. With NavaCLI: /nava trace !id.
Requests the node\'s neighbor info (last heard neighbors with SNR). Standard request — no NavaCLI equivalent.
Requests the node\'s signal/local mesh statistics (reliability, utilization). Standard request — no NavaCLI equivalent.
Requests air quality metrics (PM2.5/PM10) if the node has a sensor. Standard request — no NavaCLI equivalent.
Requests Linux host metrics (memory/CPU) if the node is a host-capable device. Standard request — no NavaCLI equivalent.
Generates the node\'s business-card URL (https://meshtastic.org/v/#...) and copies it to the clipboard, ready to share or import in another app.
no key yet — use Request key

This node\'s public key is not known yet (e.g. a card imported without a key). Requests a NodeInfo/user-info exchange so the node broadcasts its key, which is then stored in the app\'s cache for this card.
Adds a public key (base64) to the target\'s admin list, authorizing that node as a controller. Local (USB) only — remote admin needs PKC.
Sets ONLY the private key (base64, 32 bytes). At reboot the public key is regenerated from it and the node becomes the Master Node (rescue control). This changes the node\'s identity.
Requests device telemetry (battery, voltage, channel/air utilization) from the chosen node and shows the decoded response.
Requests the node\'s position. Tip: nodes with GPS disabled or position broadcasts off may not answer.
Sends a route-discovery to the node; the popup shows the path (hops and SNR). Great for checking mesh connectivity.
Changes the node\'s owner name. It also triggers a NodeInfo broadcast, which refreshes the node\'s identity in the mesh.
Applies the Good Practices presets (hop 5, NodeInfo/position every 72 h, smart position off) via read-modify-write — other settings are never corrupted.
Exports every config section (config, module config, channels) to a JSON file on the phone.
Restores a previous backup file. Tip: restore only backups taken from the same node type/firmware.
Sends the typed message to the mesh (broadcast, or to the chosen node). Keep test messages minimal on busy channels.

Hops and SNR with which the node hears you. If not in the DB it auto-launches a TraceRoute. Usage: route !ID

Blocks and silences the node, purging its public key. Usage: ign add !ID

You will block the node and its public key will be PURGED. A mistyped ID can block an admin node: unblocking with ign rm does not recover the key automatically.
Adds to favorites with hop bypass; creates an orphan RAM slot if never heard (max 10). Usage: fav add !ID
Removes from favorites. Usage: fav rm !ID
Auto-favorites direct routers (hop bypass) and registers them in RAM. Default ON. Usage: fav auto [on|off] (no argument shows the state).
Changes the name (supports quotes). Usage: set_name "Long" "Short"
Changes the hardware role. Options: client, mute, router.
Turns MQTT on/off. Options: on, off.
TX power [0-12] (Promicro/E22P). On the Faketec HT-RA62 it is [0-22].
Evicts temporary nodes keeping favorites and admins.
You will clear the learned temporary nodes (they re-learn with traffic). Favorites and admins are kept.
Empties the node database. Resend a PKI command to re-accredit admin.
Empties the ENTIRE repeater node database: you lose learned routes and contacts. You must re-accredit admin by resending a PKI command. Irreversible.
Delayed reboot in 3 s (the ACK goes out first).
Emergency factory reset restoring rescue channels.
Factory reset: wipes ALL configuration and restores rescue channels. The repeater will stop serving NavaTastic until reconfigured via the rescue network or physically. Irreversible.
Changes battery chemistry and adjusts cutoff/OCV/LPCOMP. Persists in /resilience.bin. Cutoffs: lipo 3500, nimh 3400, sodium 2600, lifepo4 2800.
Changes battery chemistry: modifies the cutoff voltage, OCV curve and power-off trigger. A wrong chemistry can drain or damage the battery and leave the node unusable until physically adjusted.
Lowering the cutoff too much can over-discharge and irreversibly damage the battery. Raising it too much powers the node off prematurely. If wrong, physical adjustment is required.
A wrong LPCOMP wake level can prevent the node from waking from solar sleep, leaving it off forever until physically recovered.
Hibernation with radio off (RTC2); wakes by timer and reboots. Hours [1-720]. Replies "MODO TORMENTA ACTIVADO..." and waits 15 s before sleeping.
Storm mode switches the radio off and hibernates the node for hours. If the timer fails, the node stays asleep until physical intervention.
Storm mode switches the radio off and hibernates the node for 60 seconds. If the timer fails, the node stays asleep until physical intervention.
Storm mode switches the radio off and hibernates the node for 120 seconds. If the timer fails, the node stays asleep until physical intervention.
Turns TX off after 3 s (keeps RX).
Turns Bluetooth off/on; schedules a real reboot (read at boot).
Turns sleep/wake announcements ([Sueño]/[Vivo]/[Listo]/[Boot]) on the Navadmin channel on/off. Persists in /resilience.bin. No argument shows the current state.
Broadcasts a message on channel 0 signed by the repeater. Usage: msg "text"
NodeInfo beacon without requesting a reply.
